name: Rapha Cycling Club (RCC)
who: Global cycling club run out of 29 Rapha Clubhouses worldwide; join via the RCC app, though new memberships are on a waitlist.
why: The clubhouse model it pioneered is now the template every apparel brand copies for cycling community.
warning: New RCC memberships were paused as of late 2025; joining is waitlist-only.

name: Bondi Icebergs Club
who: Winter ocean-swimming club at Bondi's cliff-edge pool; members swim three Sundays a month May-September to keep membership.
why: A 1929 institution with over 1,000 adult members and one of the most photographed pools on earth.

name: Serpentine Swimming Club
who: Hyde Park open-water swim club with year-round early-morning swims; the Christmas Day Peter Pan Cup is open to entrants.
why: Racing for the Peter Pan Cup every Christmas Day since 1864 makes this the longest-running fixture in open-water swimming.

name: Coney Island Polar Bear Club
who: The oldest winter bathing club in the US; members swim Sundays November-April, and the public can join the New Year's Day Plunge.
why: Founded in 1903, it turned cold-water swimming into a New York civic ritual that raised over $91K for local causes in 2026.

name: South End Rowing Club
who: Aquatic Park rowing and open-water swim club since 1873; hosts the public Alcatraz swim and the annual Bridge to Bridge Regatta.
why: One of the oldest athletic clubs in the country, kept alive by a century-plus rivalry with its Aquatic Park neighbor.

name: Dolphin Club
who: Aquatic Park swim and rowing club founded 1877, right next door to South End Rowing Club; open water swims off the boathouse daily.
why: Its decades-long friendly rivalry with South End Rowing Club is a defining piece of San Francisco open-water culture.

name: Brighton Swimming Club
who: The UK's oldest continuously running swim club, founded 1860; sea-swimming section meets daily, plus water polo and masters sections.
why: A 165-year-old club that never really stopped, except during WWII when the beaches were closed.

name: La Jolla Cove Swim Club
who: Open-water swim club at La Jolla Cove since 1916; runs the Pier to Cove Swim and the annual La Jolla Cove Swim each September.
why: A century of organizing the rough-water races that put La Jolla on the open-water swimming map.

name: Major Taylor Cycling Club (NY/NJ)
who: Newark-based chapter of the national Major Taylor club network honoring the pioneering Black champion cyclist; weekly calendar rides open to all levels.
why: Anchors a decades-old national network of clubs built around diversifying cycling, with an annual Women On Wheels century.

name: East Side Riders Bike Club
who: Community bike club based in Watts since 2008; weekly rides, bike-safety classes, and neighborhood cleanups anyone can join.
why: Built a citywide reputation as 'more than a bike club,' earning Super Bowl LVI and MLS 2024 Legacy Awards.

name: Black Girls Do Bike
who: National network of 100+ local chapters getting Black women and girls on bikes through regular group rides; join a city chapter directly.
why: Grew from one city to over 100 chapters and 170 chapter leaders, with a national meetup drawing riders across the country.

name: The Black Foxes
who: International collective of Black cyclists and outdoors people; organizes group rides and outdoor meetups, join through their events and social channels.
why: A newer crew that already has brand backing (Liv Cycling feature) for reclaiming space in outdoor sport.

name: CIBBOWS
who: Coney Island Brighton Beach Open Water Swimmers; weekly Saturday and Sunday training swims at Grimaldo's Chair, plus an annual ocean race series.
why: Twenty years of turning Brooklyn's beaches into a serious open-water training ground.

name: Chicago Tri Club
who: Social, all-levels triathlon club running swim-bike-run training sessions and a first-timer program; join through membership on their site.
why: Chicago's go-to multi-sport club, built around training toward the city's own marquee triathlon.
